data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by infrastructure issues, not security findings. The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 API errors when reviewing .gitignore and .SRCINFO, preventing completion. The openrouter/free model (advisory only) had a parsing error for .SRCINFO when it returned an unexpected format. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. These are tool failures, not substantive security disagreements.
coverage_issues: qwen model: API errors (HTTP 400) prevented review of .gitignore and .SRCINFO
openrouter/free model: parsing error for .SRCINFO due to unexpected model response format
learnings: API errors should trigger automatic retry or fallback to another model rather than marking the entire audit as inconclusive
Model response parsing should be more robust to handle unexpected formats (e.g., content safety filters returning non-standard responses)
When infrastructure errors prevent file review, the tool should distinguish between 'could not review due to error' and 'reviewed and found safe' to avoid false inconclusive verdicts
Advisory reports with parsing errors should be clearly flagged as tool failures rather than security concerns
